name: Guillotine Press
description: The guillotine press is a barbell bench press variation where the bar is lowered to the neck or upper chest rather than the mid-sternum. This higher bar contact point increases pectoralis major stretch and horizontal adduction range, shifting more of the load to the clavicular head and maximizing muscle fiber recruitment across the chest. Due to the extreme shoulder position, it carries higher injury risk and should be reserved for experienced lifters.

execution.starting_position: Lie on a flat bench under a barbell rack. Grip the bar wide (index fingers on the smooth ring or slightly outside). Position yourself so the bar tracks over the neck/clavicle area, not the mid-chest.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a spotter at all times. Use lighter weight than a standard bench press — the increased stretch significantly reduces the amount that can be safely lifted. Set safety bars.
steps: Step 1: Position on the bench so the bar will descend to the clavicle or upper chest. Grip wide with elbows flared.
Step 2: Unrack the bar and hold it above the clavicular area.
Step 3: Inhale and slowly lower the bar toward the neck/upper chest, allowing the elbows to flare to approximately 90 degrees.
Step 4: Touch the upper chest/clavicle lightly, then exhale and press back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on the descent; exhale on the press.
common_mistakes: Using the same weight as a standard bench press — reduce load significantly
Lowering too quickly, which can injure the shoulder capsule
safety_considerations: Always use a spotter and set the safety bars
Not recommended for those with existing shoulder impingement, labrum issues, or AC joint problems
This exercise carries higher injury risk than standard bench press — build shoulder health first
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Touch the upper chest or clavicle — do not bounce. Control the full descent.
coaching_cues: Let the elbows flare wide — this is intentional for this variation
Use lighter load than standard press and focus on the stretch
